name: Wetland rice cultivation at Kuahuqiao
summary: Rice was cultivated in a coastal wetland at Kuahuqiao during the Early Neolithic, as inferred from sediments and excavated rice remains.
description: At Kuahuqiao in the lower Yangtze, sediment evidence and rice remains support cultivation in a wetland where people also gathered wild foods. Researchers disagree over which vegetation was burned during the site’s earliest clearance. A barrier to regulate brackish flooding remains a hypothesis.

date.label: Approximately 7700–7550 cal BP (5750–5600 BCE)
date.basis: Zong and colleagues’ interpretation of the studied Kuahuqiao sequence. Calibrated BP uses 1950 as its reference year.

events.statement: Sediment and plant remains indicate rice cultivation in a coastal wetland at Kuahuqiao.
events.scope: Cultivation inferred for the Kuahuqiao occupation sequence studied by Zong and colleagues.
events.caveats: The date describes the studied sequence. The evidence gives no excavated field layout or exact cultivation start date.

evidence.supports: Sediment and biological indicators support rice cultivation in a managed wetland in the sampled occupation interval.
Independent morphology of excavated rice grains and husks supports early cultivation at Kuahuqiao.

earliest_record.rationale: Date of the sampled site sequence with palaeoecological evidence of wetland cultivation.

unresolved.note: The taxa targeted by burning and the existence and form of any barrier to flooding are unsettled. Seek excavated structures with stratigraphic ties to the cultivation horizon.

evidence.supports: Infers alder clearance and proposes that barriers could have regulated flooding.
Interprets separate measurements from the same locality as showing burning of oak and pine woodland.
